chapter: Teddy Wilson, Cafe Society and bebop
title: Art Tatum, too fast to understand at first
summary: He first met Tatum in Toledo with Cab, found him classical and without a beat, and only later grasped how great he was.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: And Tatum used to play at Monroe's?
Tatum, yes. Yes. Most all the piano
went by there and played, players from (unintelligible) played there.
Now how did somebody like Tatum affect you in those days? His style was --

Well I first met Tatum in Toledo, when I was with Cab. And I thought he was just amazing, I never heard a piano played like that. I thought it was amazing because it was altogether different from -- from stride piano. I thought, you know, he was -- I thought he was a classical, he sounded very classical to me, at that time.
I didn't understand too much until later on, how great he was, then I found out just how great he was. Tatum was.
It didn't really impress you too much?
It didn't at the first time, but he was so fast, you know, that I didn't get into what he was doing.
You know, the swing I wasn't used to hearing guys like Fats and the people like that, you know, with a beat --
-- and Tatum, at that time when I first heard him he didn't have a beat, but he was so fast, you
Took me a long time to figure him out. Cause things he was playing, just too fast for me to understand. At that time, but later on I began to dig him, what he was doing.
